# Hyperobjects Spec Full LLM Context

Last Updated: 2026-09-29

## Purpose

A stable, tool-agnostic map for working in this repository without depending on
vendor-specific instruction files.

## Canonical instruction order

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `README.md`
3. `llms.txt`
4. `docs/`, `.github/workflows/`, and the relevant module under `src/`

`AGENTS.md` is the source of truth. `CLAUDE.md` exists only to redirect Claude
and other legacy agent integrations to it.

## Repo boundary

PUBLIC, Apache-2.0, installed by third parties. No secrets, no credentials, no
internal hostnames or IPs, no client names, no private-repo paths, no
operational runbook content. Every rule cites a public yantra4d or
fashion-cabinet source. Cite a commons ruling by id and public effect, never by
runbook.

## Package map (`src/`)

- `y4d_spec` — the Yantra4D cartridge runner (`y4d-spec`).
  - `rules.py` — pure manifest rules. Each cites its yantra4d origin (file and
    line) in the module docstring; keeping the citation current is what makes a
    divergence from the platform visible instead of silent.
  - `semantic_rules.py` — structure of the SEM-1 semantic fields: interface
    `frame` expressions (frame grammar v1.1: `let`, degree trig, sqrt/rounding,
    comparisons, `iif`; `FRAME_GRAMMAR_VERSION`, `FRAME_GRAMMAR_MIN_KEYSTONE`),
    `let` blocks (dependency order, cycles named), vectors and symmetry,
    `polarity`, `size_key` (select or exact-value slider maps), and the
    `requirements` profile. Vocabulary membership is the lexicon's rule.
  - `frame_eval.py` — evaluates an interface frame at a parameter point
    (ASM-1 §1): full injection, `let` resolved first, a hand-walked vetted `ast`
    (no `eval`; domain errors raise), unit `normal`, orthogonalised `x_axis`,
    `Frame.homogeneous()` = H(F).
  - `frame_gate.py` / `frame_geometry.py` — the render-time frame gate (ASM-1
    §8) under `--render`: planar (progressive face-search radius, 15 mm ×1.5 to
    the half-diagonal, reported as `search_radius_mm`) or axis test per
    `geometry_type`, UNVERIFIED for the rest; a no-op for a manifest without frames.
  - `structure.py` — the on-disk rules (mode sources, escaping includes,
    vendored trees, shipped LICENSE).
  - `default_drift.py` — `default-drift`, NOTE ONLY: manifest `default` vs the
    literal the source falls back to (`PARAM(lambda: id, lit)` via ast, top-level
    `.scad` assignments, graph binding literals), per (file, line), with no mode
    scoping (GOC-1 v1.0.1 §4.1).
  - `conformance.py` — orchestration; owns the result object and the tiers.
  - `geometry.py` — CadQuery execution through the shared sandbox, the mesh bar,
    body counting, STL export.
  - [`openscad.py`](src/y4d_spec/openscad.py) — the platform's OpenSCAD command
    line and environment; preserves bounded compiler warnings/errors as notes
    even when a partial STL passes mesh checks. See [README](README.md) for the
    diagnostic limits and the notes-first policy.
  - `brep.py` — the B-Rep validity gate, run BEFORE tessellation.
  - `parity.py` — cross-kernel comparison; mirrors the platform's
    `scripts/qa/verify_parity.py` gate for gate. Also carries the GOLDEN-TWIN
    rule: `COMPARABLE_PAIRS` is `(openscad, cadquery)` and `(cadquery, graph)`,
    so a graph authored for a cartridge that already has a script must agree
    with that script at the same bar before the script may be retired.
  - `graph_render.py` — the `.graph.json` half: transpile with the vendored
    engine, then hand the emitted `.py` to `geometry.render_part`. The keystone
    authors this; the emission it calls is vendored.
  - `graph/` — **VENDORED, byte-identical, never hand-edit.** A copy of
    yantra4d's `apps/api/services/engine/graph_engine.py` plus
    `packages/schemas/graph.schema.json` and `graph-node-catalog.json`, pinned
    by sha256 in `graph.lock.json`, enforced by
    `scripts/qa/check_graph_sync.py` (blocking; `--update` re-pins), documented
    in `VENDORED.md`, and excluded from ruff because reformatting would break
    the hash. Change the platform and re-vendor. Do NOT bump SPEC_PIN as part
    of a re-vendor. The platform's `spec-conformance` asserts the reverse
    direction, so neither repo can drift alone.
  - `printability.py` — measurements, never failures; every threshold
    provisional.
  - `render_environment.py` — the render environment as data.
  - `cli.py` — argument surface and the `rules` explainer.
  - `assembly/` — ASM-1 type-level assemblies: `validate_assembly(doc,
    resolver)` (schema, resolution, mating rule, BFS placement, closure of
    every mate, reachability, `hyperobjects-assembly-v1` digest), the
    `ComponentResolver` protocol and its commons / standard-parts / external
    resolvers, and `y4d-spec assembly check`. See `docs/ASSEMBLIES.md`.
    Continuous-symmetry closing mates compare the stated `angle_deg` (0.5.0);
    a producer's `capability_profile` is checked against the vocabulary
    (`process` is a list). ASM-1 §9 (v1.3, 0.7.0): `kinematics.py` (joints on
    mates — driven, follower, passive — machine-axis bindings, the Halton pose
    sweep), `paths.py` (belt paths: pitch-line length, planarity), `sweep.py`
    (the sweep's findings), `posing.py` (`pose()`, `pose_from_axes()`, golden
    pose files with the toFixed(6) number format). pravara never computes
    kinematics (owner decision D4): the keystone is the reference, the viewer
    reproduces the golden poses.
- `hyperobjects_aas.assembly` / `hyperobjects_aas.resolver` — ASM-1 §5: a checked
  assembly → one AAS Environment (shell `aas/assembly/{slug}/{digest16}/p{N}`;
  AssemblyDocument, HSEBoM BillOfMaterials, Mates, AssemblyPlacement, Kinematics
  (ASM-1 §9, projection version 2), IDTA 02020
  CapabilityDescription, RequirementProfile roll-up), and the resolver that
  reads stored type shells back so a service (asset-shells, ASM-1 §6)
  re-derives the same digest and environment. `y4d-spec aas build
  <assemblies/slug>`.
- `fc_spec` — the Fashion Cabinet contracts (`fc-spec`).
- `bridge_check` — the FC↔Yantra4D hardware-link handshake (`ho-bridge`).
- `commons_sandbox` — the restricted-execution core both platforms run
  cartridges through. Defense in depth, NOT a security boundary on its own.
- `hyperobjects_schemas` — every bundled JSON Schema, plus the identity key.
  - `generator_output.py` — GOC-1 (`variables.json`): `canonical_json`,
    `variables_sha256`, `tree_sha256` (`hyperobjects-tree-v1`), `instance_id`,
    `check_generator_output`; the body of `y4d-spec bundle check` and
    `fc-spec check generator-output`.
- `hyperobjects_lexicon` — the Commons Lexicon corpus, the controlled
  vocabularies, the fabrication vocabularies (SEM-1 §4: processes, material
  classes, process parameters, machine capabilities, interface sizes) and their
  manifest-membership rule, the article contract, the dictionary tools and the
  reader. See docs/FABRICATION_VOCABULARIES.md.
- `hyperobjects_aas` — the SEM-1 AAS v3.1 projection (`aas build|build-material|
  check` on both CLIs). `ids.py` is the permanent id scheme (`id.madfam.io`);
  every shell and submodel id carries `PROJECTION_VERSION` (`…/{rev16}/p{N}`,
  also the shell's `ProjectionVersion` extension), and `drift.py` + the golden
  refresh `--check` refuse changed bytes under a minted id without a bump;
  `templates.py` holds the IDTA identifiers (copied, with source paths) and the
  conformance-claim rule; `concepts.py` builds ConceptDescriptions from the
  lexicon; `solid.py` / `soft.py` / `material.py` are the projections;
  `check.py` validates. `schemas/aas.json` is VENDORED (CC-BY-4.0, lock +
  hash test) — never edit it.
- `hyperobjects_standard_parts` — the standard-parts catalog (ASM-1 §4): one
  cited JSON entry per COTS part (`parts/{key}.json`, schema
  `standard-part.schema.json`), interfaces in the SEM-1 §2.3 shape, the loader,
  `resolve_parameters`, `interface_frames`, `part_digest`, and the catalog lane
  (third verdict of `vocab`). See docs/STANDARD_PARTS.md.

## Durable contracts

**The render environment is single-source.** `y4d_spec/render_environment.py`
owns the OpenSCAD version, the AppImage SHA-256, the apt set and the fonts
policy. The platform image, the commons CI and the CI runner image all read it
rather than keeping their own copy; three copies of a version number is three
chances to drift, and the drift reads as the cartridge being broken. Never add a
fourth copy — read `y4d-spec render-env --openscad-version`. The pin is a FLOOR:
BOSL2 v2.0.753 does not render below `2026.02.13`.

**Both engines are judged.** A mode that declares both a `.py`/`.cq` and a
`.scad` renders and is judged on both sides. The platform serves only one, so
the other is exercised by nothing else.

**Parity is per-cartridge.** `--render --parity` compares the two kernels of
every dual-engine target that rendered on both: AABB extents, volume,
placement, shape. Placement and shape are separate numbers because extents and
volume cannot tell "same part, different origin" from "different part".

**Exemptions are visible debt.** A per-part parity exemption or a widened
tolerance requires a non-empty `reason`, enforced with no `--render` at all —
otherwise a cartridge could switch off the check by switching off the
comparison. Exemptions are counted separately (`exempt=`) so they cannot shrink
the denominator.

**A declared parameter must reach geometry.** Every `parameters[].id` is
referenced by a source of a mode that lists it, or the cartridge fails
(G-DEADPARAM). `.py`/`.cq` by the bare identifier — parameters are injected as
bare globals, so `PARAM(lambda: x, d)` counts because `x` is in it and `PARAM`
is a cartridge idiom rather than the accessor; `.scad` by a use outside the
identifier's own declaration line, because OpenSCAD accepts an unknown `-D` in
silence and the declaration is the thing being overridden; `.graph.json` by a
`parameters[].binding` naming a node param. Judged only against the modes that
list the parameter. A reference in a library the cartridge SHIPS counts;
unresolvable includes are skipped, never assumed. `target_part` is exempt.
`intentionally_unused: {"reason": …}` allow-lists one, reason required and
non-empty — visible debt, same convention as a parity exemption.

**The generator-output schema lives here only.** `generator-output.schema.json`
(GOC-1) and its four algorithms are owned by this package; platforms import them
and keep no copy. Changing a digest algorithm forks every producer, so the golden
vectors in `tests/test_generator_output.py` change only with a contract version.
The document carries no physical (material/process/slicer/printer) settings.

**AAS conformance is computed, never asserted.** A submodel carries an IDTA
template semanticId only when every element that template marks mandatory is
present (matched by semanticId); otherwise the MADFAM template id, with the IDTA
id as a supplemental pointer. `aas check` fails an over-claim. A BaSyx
round-trip that did not run is reported as `basyx=not installed`, not as a pass.

**A shell id names a revision AND a projection version.** Shells and submodels
are `…/{rev16}/p{N}` with `N` = `hyperobjects_aas.PROJECTION_VERSION` (also the
shell's `ProjectionVersion` extension). Stores keep ids immutable (409 on new
bytes), so a projection change that moves the bytes for the same inputs MUST bump
the version; the golden drift guard (`scripts/refresh_assembly_golden.py --check`,
`tests/test_projection_version.py`) fails until it does. Asset, concept,
template and standard-part ids carry no version.

**A skip is never a pass.** `renders=` counts meshes actually judged and
`skipped=` counts the rest; `--require-openscad` turns a missing binary from a
skip into a failure so a lane that rendered nothing cannot report green.

**Generated artefacts are committed.** `docs/reader/` and the count blocks in
`README.md` are built from the corpus and checked byte-for-byte in CI
(`fc-spec reader --check`, `scripts/refresh_reader_counts.py --check`). Rebuild
them in the same commit as any corpus, vocabulary or snapshot change.

**Geometry tests skip, never fail.** They carry `@pytest.mark.geometry` and
`conftest.py` skips them when the CAD kernel cannot import. Put
`pytest.importorskip` BEFORE any module-scope `numpy`/`trimesh` import or the
run is interrupted at collection instead of skipping. CI installs the extra and
fails the job when `geometry_available()` is False, so nothing skips there.

## Local development

    python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[geometry,dev]"
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest -ra
    .venv/bin/ruff check src tests

Python 3.11+. The `[geometry]` extra pulls a CAD kernel (~400 MB) and on
Debian/Ubuntu additionally needs `libgl1`, `libglib2.0-0` and `libxrender1`.
Manifest-only work needs none of it and runs in under a second.
